page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-32GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It is equipped with 16 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of performance characteristics. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance in Geekbench, scoring 2197.0, and top-tier text processing capabilities. However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 785.99, and multi-core CPU performance sits in the middle 50% at 10921.94. Memory bandwidth tests show average speeds for cached small blocks but drop to the bottom 25% for uncached large-block read and write operations. Additionally, medium-model LLM text generation is limited, registering in the bottom 10% at 4.74 tokens per second.

The shared CPU allocation model presents a clear tradeoff, offering a high core count at a lower resource density cost, though it introduces susceptibility to host-level CPU contention. This profile is suited for workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution but do not require sustained, isolated CPU performance. Appropriate use cases include static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and general-purpose multi-threaded tasks that can tolerate shared-resource variability.
